title: Uber turns its best AI engineers loose on the rest of the business
excerpt: Uber's new AI strategy sends top engineers into every department to rethink workflows and uncover productivity gains.
content_html:
After starting the tokenmaxxing panic, Uber's CTO is back with a very different AI story

By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

Remember the executive who sparked the tokenmaxxing panic earlier this year after saying Uber had already blown through its 2026 budget for Anthropic's Claude Code? He's back with a more interesting lesson about AI.

Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga says the company has started sending its best AI engineers into departments like finance, legal, marketing, customer support, HR, and procurement to study how people actually work before building AI tools with them.

He called these two-week teams "Agentic Pods." Engineers spend the first few days shadowing employees, learning every step of a workflow, then quickly build and test software to improve it.

The results are striking. One financial planning process dropped from 15 hours to 30 minutes. Financial reports fell from two days to 10 minutes. Marketing quality checks shrank from two weeks to less than an hour.

Naga said the biggest gains rarely come from speeding up one task. They come from redesigning an entire workflow around AI, eliminating unnecessary approvals, replacing old software, and helping people make decisions faster. You can see this at work here, too.

Several tech executives compared the approach to Silicon Valley's fast-growing "forward-deployed engineer" role. The twist? Instead of sending these AI experts to customers, Uber is deploying them inside its own business to find the next wave of productivity gains.

Peter Wilczynski, chief product officer at Vantortech, jokingly dubbed the role the "Rearward Deployed Engineer," describing engineers embedded deep inside corporate operations to redesign entire workflows around AI rather than simply speeding up individual tasks.

在引发代币最大化恐慌后，Uber 的首席技术官带着一个截然不同的人工智能故事回来了

作者：Alistair Barr 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 《技术备忘录》时事通讯的作者

还记得今年早些时候，一位高管在表示 Uber 已经超支了 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 的 2026 年预算后引发了 tokenmaxxing 恐慌吗？ 他带着关于人工智能的更有趣的课程回来了。

Uber 首席技术官 Praveen Neppalli Naga 表示，该公司已开始将最优秀的人工智能工程师派遣到财务、法律、营销、客户支持、人力资源和采购等部门，研究人们的实际工作方式，然后再使用他们构建人工智能工具。

他将这些为期两周的团队称为“Agentic Pods”。 工程师在最初的几天里跟踪员工，学习工作流程的每一步，然后快速构建和测试软件以改进它。

结果是惊人的。 一项财务规划流程从 15 小时缩短到 30 分钟。 财务报告从两天缩短到十分钟。 营销质量检查从两周缩短到不到一个小时。

纳加表示，最大的收获很少来自于加快一项任务的速度。 它们来自于围绕人工智能重新设计整个工作流程、消除不必要的审批、替换旧软件以及帮助人们更快地做出决策。 您也可以在这里看到这一点。

几位科技高管将这种方法与硅谷快速增长的“前沿部署工程师”角色进行了比较。 转折？ Uber 没有将这些人工智能专家派往客户那里，而是将他们部署在自己的企业内部，以寻找下一波生产力提升的机会。

Vantortech 首席产品官 Peter Wilczynski 开玩笑地将这一角色称为“后部部署工程师”，描述工程师深入公司运营，围绕人工智能重新设计整个工作流程，而不是简单地加快单个任务的速度。
